definitions.explanation: Describes something that has an air of mystery or is hard to understand. Derived from the verb 謎めく (to seem mysterious) in its past/attributive form.

examples.japanese: {謎|なぞ}めいた{笑|え}みを{浮|う}かべた。
{彼|かれ}は{謎|なぞ}めいた{言葉|ことば}を{残|のこ}して{去|さ}った。
examples.english: He left behind mysterious words and departed.

examples.japanese: その{島|しま}には{謎|なぞ}めいた{遺跡|いせき}がいくつも{残|のこ}されている。
examples.english: Several enigmatic ruins remain on the island.

notes:
USAGE:
Always used before a noun to modify it. Gives a literary or atmospheric quality to descriptions. Common in novels, mystery stories, and evocative writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {謎|なぞ}めいた{笑|え}み (enigmatic smile)
- {謎|なぞ}めいた{言葉|ことば} (mysterious words)
- {謎|なぞ}めいた{雰囲気|ふんいき} (mysterious atmosphere)
- {謎|なぞ}めいた{人物|じんぶつ} (mysterious person)

GRAMMAR:
Derived from {謎|なぞ}めく (to seem mysterious, godan verb with the suffix めく). The た form is used as a pre-noun modifier. The base verb {謎|なぞ}めく can also be used predicatively: {何|なに}か{謎|なぞ}めいている (there is something mysterious about it).
